title: Najmeh Amini Faces Death Sentence and Over 12 Years in Prison Following Arrest During January Protests
content:
According to HRANA, Najmeh Amini is currently being held in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad.

A source close to Amini’s family confirmed this information and told HRANA about the judicial proceedings in her cases: “Following her arrest, she faced two separate legal cases, one heard by the Mashhad Revolutionary Court and the other by Criminal Court One. In the case heard by Criminal Court One, she was sentenced to death on charges of ‘insulting the Prophet.’ Initially, the charge against Ms. Amini in this case was described as ‘insulting the Imams,’ but the charge was subsequently changed during the judicial proceedings.”

The source added: “In a separate case, Branch One of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court sentenced Ms. Amini to a total of 12 years, six months, and one day in prison on charges including ‘acting against national security’ and ‘propaganda against the regime.'”
snippet: According to HRANA, Najmeh Amini is currently being held in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Report on the Execution of a Prisoner in Sepidar Prison, Ahvaz
content:
According to HRANA, the news agency of Human Rights Activists in Iran, a prisoner’s death sentence was carried out at Sepidar Prison in Ahvaz.

HRANA has confirmed the identity of the prisoner as Seyed Sadegh Mousavi, 43, married, father of one child, and a resident of Ramshir County. His execution was carried out on August 24, 2026.

Based on information received by HRANA, Mr. Mousavi was arrested approximately four years ago on murder charges and subsequently sentenced to death by a criminal court.

At the time of this report, his execution has not been announced by prison officials or the relevant authorities.

According to HRA’s Annual Report, in 2025 at least 2,063 citizens, including 61 women and 2 juvenile offenders, were executed. Of these, the sentences of 11 individuals were carried out in public. During the same period, 172 other individuals were sentenced to death.
snippet: According to HRANA, the news agency of Human Rights Activists in Iran, a prisoner’s death sentence was carried out at Sepidar Prison in Ahvaz.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Two Individuals Arrested by Security Forces in Baneh
content:
According to HRANA, citing Kurdpa, Yousef Rahimi and Azad Rahmati were arrested in Baneh.

According to the report, security forces arrested the two men at their respective homes on Wednesday, September 23, without presenting a judicial warrant.

At the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the reasons for their arrest, their whereabouts, or the charges brought against them.

Azad Rahmati is married, has children, and is active in environmental issues. Yousef Rahimi is the head of the Haje Cultural and Literary Association.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Kurdpa, Yousef Rahimi and Azad Rahmati were arrested in Baneh.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Mohammad Ahmadi Sentenced to 16 Years in Prison
content:
According to HRANA, Mohammad Ahmadi, a prisoner held in Greater Tehran Prison, has been sentenced to imprisonment.

Based on information received by HRANA, Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court sentenced Mr. Ahmadi to 16 years in prison on charges of “espionage.” The verdict was communicated to him in prison.

Ahmadi was arrested by security forces amid war-related security developments and subsequently transferred to Greater Tehran Prison.

HRANA is continuing its investigation into the details of his case, including the evidence cited by the court and whether he has had access to a lawyer of his choosing.
snippet: According to HRANA, Mohammad Ahmadi, a prisoner held in Greater Tehran Prison, has been sentenced to imprisonment.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Mohammad Naderi Sentenced to Death
content:
According to HRANA, Mohammad Naderi, a prisoner held in Greater Tehran Prison, has been sentenced to death.

Based on information received by HRANA, Naderi was sentenced to death by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court on charges of “espionage.”

He was arrested by security forces amid war-related security developments and transferred to Greater Tehran Prison.

HRANA’s investigation into the details of his case, including the evidence cited by the court and whether he has had access to a lawyer of his choosing, is ongoing.
snippet: According to HRANA, Mohammad Naderi, a prisoner held in Greater Tehran Prison, has been sentenced to death.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Nine Attorneys in Gilan Sentenced to Prison
content:
According to HRANA, nine attorneys in Gilan Province have been sentenced to prison in connection with a joint case.

Masoumeh Pourshahrani, Tahereh Pour Esmaeili, Shadi Falahati, Gholamhossein Layeghi, Hesam Ahmadpour, Ladan Asefi-Rad, Mohammadreza Tak, Kian Taherajaroud, and Dalili (first name unknown) were each sentenced by Branch 2 of the Rasht Revolutionary Court to seven months and 15 days in prison on the charge of “propaganda against the regime” and 12 months in prison on the charge of “insulting the Supreme Leader and the founder of the Islamic Republic.”

Based on information received by HRANA, the sentences were issued against the attorneys recently. Another part of their case, concerning the charge of “insulting the sacred,” is also under review by Branch 2 of the Rasht Criminal Court.

Hesam Pourahmadi, Masoumeh Pourshahrani, and Tahereh Pour Esmaeili were arrested by security forces in Rasht during the second week of September 2025 and transferred to Lakan Prison in the city. The three attorneys were released on bail several days later.
snippet: According to HRANA, nine attorneys in Gilan Province have been sentenced to prison in connection with a joint case.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Teachers’ Union Activist Hossein Salami Sentenced to One Year in Prison
content:
According to HRANA, citing the Coordinating Council of Iranian Teachers’ Trade Associations, Hossein Salami has been sentenced to prison.

According to the report, Salami was sentenced to one year in prison on charges of “propaganda against the regime” and “disturbing public opinion.”

The report states that the charges stem, in part, from Salami’s union and social activities, as well as certain statements he made regarding events related to the 2022 protests and the poisoning of school students.

Hossein Salami, a teachers’ union activist residing in Mazandaran Province, has previously faced security-related measures and arrest.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing the Coordinating Council of Iranian Teachers’ Trade Associations, Hossein Salami has been sentenced to prison.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Attorney Hamid Rahmani Manshadi Remains in Detention After Two Weeks in Yazd
content:
According to HRANA, Hamid Rahmani Manshadi, an attorney and law professor at Yazd University, remains in detention.

Based on information received by HRANA, Rahmani was arrested by security forces in Yazd approximately two weeks ago, following a court summons and his subsequent appearance in court. His whereabouts remain unknown. Throughout his detention, he has been denied visits with his family and access to legal counsel.

At the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the reasons for his arrest or the charges brought against him.

Hamid Rahmani Manshadi, 45, is an attorney and law professor at Yazd University.
snippet: According to HRANA, Hamid Rahmani Manshadi, an attorney and law professor at Yazd University, remains in detention.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Arghavan Fallahi’s Death Sentence Overturned by Supreme Court
content:
According to HRANA, citing Emtedad, the Supreme Court has overturned Arghavan Fallahi’s death sentence.

According to the report, her request for a retrial was under review by the Supreme Court, which accepted the objections and legal challenges raised in her case. Following the approval of her retrial request, the execution of her death sentence has been suspended, and her case will be referred to another branch of the court of equal standing for reconsideration.

Previously, the Supreme Court had rejected Arghavan Fallahi’s request for a retrial.

In July of this year, the political prisoner was sentenced to death on the charge of “baghi” (armed rebellion) by Judge Abolghasem Salavati, head of Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. In late August, her death sentence was upheld by Branch 41 of the Supreme Court.

Arghavan Fallahi, aged approximately 25, was arrested by security forces in late January 2025 and transferred to the Ministry of Intelligence’s detention facility, known as Ward 209 of Evin Prison.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Emtedad, the Supreme Court has overturned Arghavan Fallahi’s death sentence.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Attorney Hassan Younesi Sentenced to Prison and Additional Punishments
content:
According to HRANA, Hassan Younesi has been sentenced to prison and additional punishments.

According to the verdict issued by Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, he was sentenced to one year in prison on the charge of “propaganda against the regime” and two years in prison on the charge of “spreading falsehoods.” He was also ordered to pay a fine of 50 million tomans and was sentenced to a ban on online activity and confiscation of his mobile phone.

Mr. Younesi also wrote that his statements regarding the events of January 7 and 8, in connection with the January 2026 protests, were among the grounds for the charges against him.

A hearing on Mr. Younesi’s charges was held before the aforementioned branch on August 10, 2026.

Previously, an interrogation session for the attorney had been held at the Culture and Media Prosecutor’s Office. According to Mr. Younesi, the case was opened following a complaint filed against him by a security agency.

Hassan Younesi, an attorney and one of those arrested during the nationwide protests of 2022, has previously been summoned and arrested in connection with his activities.
snippet: According to HRANA, Hassan Younesi has been sentenced to prison and additional punishments.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Baha’i Citizen Romina Goli Sentenced to Prison and Social Restrictions
content:
According to HRANA, Romina Goli, a Baha’i citizen, has been sentenced to prison and deprivation of social rights.

According to a verdict issued by Branch 2 of the Sari Revolutionary Court and communicated to Ms. Goli, she was sentenced to five years in prison and 10 years of deprivation of social rights on the charge of “deviant educational or proselytizing activity contrary to or disruptive of the sacred law of Islam,” under Article 500 bis of the Islamic Penal Code. She was also sentenced to seven months and 16 days in prison on the charge of “propaganda against the regime,” under Article 500 of the Islamic Penal Code.

Romina Goli was arrested by security forces in Sari on May 9, 2026. At the time of her arrest, her home was searched, and officers confiscated several personal digital devices and religious books related to the Baha’i Faith.

On May 10, Ms. Goli’s interrogation session was held at the Sari Prosecutor’s Office. She was subsequently released from prison on bail.
snippet: According to HRANA, Romina Goli, a Baha’i citizen, has been sentenced to prison and deprivation of social rights.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Turkish Aid Worker Residing in Germany, Serkan Eren, Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison in Iran
content:
According to HRANA, citing Deutsche Welle Persian, Serkan Eren, an aid worker and Turkish citizen residing in Germany, has been sentenced to 10 years in prison by a court in Iran.

STELP, a Stuttgart-based aid organization, said the sentence was issued against Mr. Eren in connection with the charge of “having ties with a hostile country.”

According to the report, Serkan Eren traveled to Iran on June 24, 2025, as a humanitarian aid worker to distribute donated supplies from Germany. He intended to leave Iran that same day, but contact with his family was cut off, and he has remained in detention ever since.

STELP protested the sentence, describing the punishment as disproportionate to the circumstances of the case. The organization said that, in order to protect the safety of Serkan Eren and others involved, it would not release further details about the case at this time.

The organization also said that, given Mr. Eren’s Turkish citizenship, it is in contact with Turkish authorities to follow up on his situation and secure his return.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Deutsche Welle Persian, Serkan Eren, an aid worker and Turkish citizen residing in Germany, has been sentenced to 10 years in prison by a court in Iran.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Report on the Execution of Four Prisoners at Sepidar Prison in Ahvaz
content:
According to HRANA, at least four prisoners were executed at Sepidar Prison in Ahvaz.

On September 16, Nemat Maghami, a resident of Maragheh, and Hossein Ghazlavi, a resident of Ahvaz, both of whom had been sentenced to death on murder charges, were executed at this prison.

According to information received by HRANA, Karim Mojdam was also executed at this prison on Monday, September 21, and Jalil Salamat, a resident of Ahvaz, was executed there on Tuesday, September 22.

Mr. Salamat was arrested six years ago in connection with a murder case at a marketplace in Ahvaz’s Hasirabad neighborhood and was ultimately sentenced to death. Mr. Mojdam was also arrested approximately four years ago on a murder charge and sentenced to death.

As of the time of this report, the executions of these prisoners have not been announced by prison officials or the relevant authorities.

According to HRA’s Annual Report, in 2025 at least 2,063 citizens, including 61 women and 2 juvenile offenders, were executed. Of these, the sentences of 11 individuals were carried out in public. During the same period, 172 other individuals were sentenced to death.
snippet: According to HRANA, at least four prisoners were executed at Sepidar Prison in Ahvaz.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Abbas Shaverdi, 17-Year-Old Teenager, Arrested in Shadegan
content:
According to HRANA, the news agency of Human Rights Activists in Iran, Abbas Shaverdi, a 17-year-old teenager, has been arrested in Shadegan, Khuzestan province.

Based on information received by HRANA, the teenager was arrested by security forces at his home in Shadegan on Friday, September 18, 2026.

At the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding the reasons for his arrest, his whereabouts, or the charges brought against him.
snippet: According to HRANA, the news agency of Human Rights Activists in Iran, Abbas Shaverdi, a 17-year-old teenager, has been arrested in Shadegan, Khuzestan province.
